content.value:
You now know subsystems, commands, button bindings, and MotorEx.

This lesson combines them into a complete TeleOp — a mecanum drive system controlled with gamepad sticks, using MotorEx for velocity control, plus button-triggered commands.

Open MecanumDriveSubsystem.java.

Declare four private MotorEx fields.

In the constructor, create each with new MotorEx(hardwareMap, "name").

Add a drive() method with forward, strafe, and turn parameters — apply the mecanum formula from the gamepad input lesson.

Add stop() to set all motors to 0.

steps.title: Set up the TeleOp in initialize()

content.value:
In MecanumTeleOpOpMode's initialize(), create your MecanumDriveSubsystem and a GamepadEx from gamepad1.

Create a RunCommand that reads the gamepad sticks (forward = -leftY, strafe = leftX, turn = rightX) and calls subsystem.drive().

Use schedule() to run it.

Add button bindings for A and B — whenPressed() with InstantCommands for telemetry and stop.

Start the OpMode and drive with the virtual gamepad.

Left stick controls forward/back and strafe.

Right stick controls turn.

Press A and B to trigger your button bindings.

This is the pattern real FTC teams use — subsystems own hardware, commands drive the robot, and the scheduler manages it all.
